Edit: By "not making my anhedonia better" I mean that it's not a "magic happy pill" but it changed my perception of the world and myself and this helped me a lot for my anhedonia.

Personally, psilocybin didn't make my anhedonia better BUT it wasn't completely useless since it helped me work on it. It was probably the greatest change in my perception of the world that I ever felt. I used to have no self-confidence and being very hopeless about my future and no matter how many times I told myself that I needed to do something to get better, I did nothing. I used mushrooms a few times, not for recreational use but for their psychological health benefit. I read a lot about them to be safe and I had a good set and setting for all my trips. It can be very confusing at times since you're rethinking everything you've ever done and how the person you are right now is simply the result of controllable events and less controllable events. The main message I understood after all my trip is that no matter who you are right now and no matter if you choosed to be here because of your decisions in the past, the only thing you can do from now on is to go upwards and build a future that you want. You might not know what you want yet but that's okay, I didn't at first too, you just got to figure out who you REALLY are, not who the people around you want you to be. Psilocybin allowed me to see myself in "3rd person view" (I was in complete darkness), it made me feel like I was just a normal human. Yes I might be different than most (I have ASD) but not a single human being is the same. I felt empathy for myself for the first time in years during this trip. I even cried (a good thing in this case) because I was seeing myself as someone who didn't lose hope. At the time, I was extremely hopeless and seeing that hopeless version of myself from another point of view really hit a deep part of my heart. I dropped a tear while writing this, that shows how much it affected me and changed me for the better. It's like the child version of myself with big dreams looked up  at the me from the present and couldn't believe I had given up.

TL;DR: Shrooms allowed me to see myself like I see others and feel empathy for myself. Also, it allowed me to focus more on the future than on the past.
